overview: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn and City Councilor Richard Caraviello participated in a debate hosted by the Medford Chamber of Commerce to discuss key municipal issues ahead of the 2023 election.

items.title: Opening Remarks and Introductions
items.summary: Medford Chamber of Commerce President Rocco DiRico and moderator Jim Morelli opened the debate, introduced the panel of journalists and community members, and outlined the rules.

items.title: Opening Statements
items.summary: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn highlighted her administration's progress on infrastructure and master planning, while City Councilor Richard Caraviello argued for new leadership to address unfilled staff positions, road repairs, and city services.

items.title: Top Priority for Next Term
items.summary: Councilor Richard Caraviello identified filling municipal staff vacancies as his top priority, while Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn focused on implementing housing production and master plans to address affordability.

items.title: Property Taxes and Proposition 2 1/2 Overrides
items.summary: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn stated a debt exclusion will be necessary for a new high school while exploring funding options for a fire station, whereas Councilor Richard Caraviello advocated for rehabilitating the existing high school and assessing overall fiscal priorities.

items.title: Employee Wages and Union Contract Negotiations
items.summary: Councilor Richard Caraviello urged prompt in-person contract negotiations funded by new development growth, while Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn defended her record of settling multiple union contracts responsibly within statutory tax limits.

items.title: Lightning Round: Challenges, Accomplishments, and Public Transit
items.summary: The candidates briefly addressed top city challenges, personal proudest municipal achievements, and advocacy for MBTA service and safety upgrades.

items.title: Traffic Safety and Transportation Infrastructure
items.summary: Councilor Richard Caraviello attributed traffic congestion and road hazards to external rideshares and delivery vehicles, while Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn cited ongoing intersection safety improvements, bike infrastructure, and Complete Streets planning.

items.title: Vision for Medford Square
items.summary: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn outlined upcoming development RFPs for city-owned parcels and waterfront activation, while Councilor Richard Caraviello proposed directly assisting property owners, adding greenery, and hiring a full-time economic development director.

items.title: Affordable Housing
items.summary: Councilor Richard Caraviello criticized delayed 40B developments and called for strict short-term rental enforcement, while Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn highlighted rising commercial growth, the creation of an Affordable Housing Trust, and ongoing housing authority projects.

items.title: Charter Review
items.summary: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn expressed support for term limits and the ongoing Charter Review Committee, while Councilor Richard Caraviello raised concerns about the committee's demographic representation and supported expanding city council authority.

items.title: High School Safety and Police Role
items.summary: Councilor Richard Caraviello supported placing law enforcement officers in school corridors to ensure safety, while Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn highlighted new high school leadership, mental health resources, and a ten-point safety plan.

items.title: Wellington Circle Development and Air Rights
items.summary: Both candidates supported multi-use development, commercial spaces, and housing using the air rights over Wellington T station, while noting traffic mitigation needs.

items.title: Lightning Round: Governance, Leaf Blowers, and Leadership
items.summary: The candidates shared brief stances on improving mayor-council communications, regulating gas-powered leaf blowers, and key personal leadership traits.

items.title: Climate Crisis and Local Resilience
items.summary: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn highlighted implementation of the city's Climate Action Plan, grant-funded community liaisons, and emergency site planning, while Councilor Richard Caraviello advocated for green infrastructure requirements and expanding environmental education.

items.title: Post-Pandemic Budgeting and Expiring Federal Relief Funds
items.summary: Councilor Richard Caraviello criticized ARPA spending choices and requested an independent audit, while Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn explained plans to transition relief-funded personnel to long-term revenue sources.

items.title: Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Outreach
items.summary: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn noted the appointment of a Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Director, expanded community events, and hiring milestones, while Councilor Richard Caraviello urged filling key staff roles and expanding multi-language translation.

items.title: Civil Discourse and Political Polarization
items.summary: Councilor Richard Caraviello commended improved civility on the city council, while Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn emphasized community resilience, public volunteerism, and shared local values.

items.title: Closing Statements
items.summary: Councilor Richard Caraviello urged voters to choose new leadership to resolve contract delays and staff vacancies, while Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn requested reelection to build upon her administration's planning, hires, and infrastructure investments.
